claims.claim: OLMoE: a fully open, state-of-the-art sparse MoE language model (1B active / 7B total)
claims.quote: We introduce OLM O E, a fully open, state-of-the-art language model leveraging
We pretrain it on 5 trillion tokens and further adapt it to create OLM O E-1B-7B-I NSTRUCT.

claims.claim: Instruction/preference-tuned OLMoE-1B-7B-Instruct exceeds larger instruct models
claims.quote: find exceeds various larger instruct models including Llama2-13B-Chat [183], OLMo-7B-Instruct

claims.claim: MoEs train ~2x faster than dense LMs with equivalent active parameters
claims.quote: Our experiments show that MoEs train ∼2× faster than dense LMs
claims.ablation_quote: Apart from MoE-related changes, we train both with the same configuration for 130B tokens.

claims.claim: Fine-grained routing with 64 small experts, 8 active, is critical
claims.quote: One critical design decision for making MoEs performant is the use of fine-grained routing with granular experts [42]: we employ 64 small experts in each layer
claims.ablation_quote: We vary the number of experts in tandem with the FFN dimension to ensure that active and total parameters and thus compute cost remain the same.

claims.claim: Dropless token-choice routing outperforms expert-choice routing
claims.quote: we find dropless [58] token-based routing [154] outperforms expert-based routing [219]
claims.ablation_quote: Both models have an 8-expert MoE in every 2nd layer. For TC, 2 experts are activated per token

claims.quote: Our findings also include those that challenge prior work, such as the ineffectiveness of shared experts
claims.ablation_quote: While both settings lead to similar performance, sharing an expert performs slightly worse.

claims.claim: Sparse upcycling from a dense model has limited benefits except at small compute budgets
claims.quote: challenge prior work, such as the ineffectiveness of shared experts [42] and the limited benefits of sparsely
claims.ablation_quote: We find that after 500B tokens, an otherwise equivalent MoE trained from scratch already catches up with the upcycled model

claims.claim: Routing analysis: early router saturation, rare co-activation, domain and vocabulary specialization
claims.quote: analyze the routing behavior in OLM O E-1B-7B, finding that routing saturates early in pretraining, experts are rarely co-activated

claims.claim: Open release of code, intermediate checkpoints, logs and training data
claims.quote: We release training code, intermediate checkpoints (every 5000 steps), training logs, and training data under open-source licenses

coding.note: Claims are taken from the abstract and introduction only. Load balancing loss, router z-loss, QK-Norm and the other settings in Table 1 and §4 also have controlled ablations, but the introduction does not state them as key contributions, so they are not coded as claims. The upcycling comparison matches the new-token budget, but the upcycled model starts from a 2T-token dense checkpoint. I still coded it YES because the authors call it 'otherwise equivalent'. Table 4 has 17 comparators. Llama3.2-1B and DCLM-1B were dropped because of the 15-model cap. The AlpacaEval leaderboard mention compares the authors' own score with leaderboard entries; it is not an independent evaluation of OLMoE, so third_party is NO. No seeds or run-to-run variance are reported.
